_comment: Velocities are APC40 mkII palette indices (palette.json). 'pairs' are [on, dim, playing-secondary] velocity triples; the hue families the packs speak (red..magenta, in hue order) take pairs[i % len(pairs)]. 'playing' is the secondary animation laid over every 'on' pad. 'ambient' fills pads Resolume leaves dark. 'touch' answers a pad press with one-shot flashes (step = seconds between rings, so a 1/8 flash of 0.5 s at 60 bpm over a 0.25 s step is a ring two pads wide; spread = seconds a sparkle burst lasts, default 0.35). 'div' rates are note values at the clock tempo (protocol.DEFAULT_BPM unless you change it): 1/2 is two beats (2 s at 60 bpm), the slowest the controller offers. 'rate' on an ambient is software steps per second. Everything was slowed on 2026-10-23 after the performer watched the first rates on a real APC40 mkII and found them 'a bit too fast'.

pack.name: Pack colours
pack.blurb: Resolume's own feedback, untouched: green for playing, dim green for loaded, one hue per layer. The baseline every other theme re-colours.

halloween.name: Halloween
halloween.blurb: Pumpkin, violet and slime. Playing pads breathe slowly between orange and purple; empty pads gutter like candles; a press sends a violet ring through the grid.

christmas.name: Christmas
christmas.blurb: Red, green and gold on a slow marquee chase around the empty pads; a press throws a gold star outward.

valentine.name: Valentine's
valentine.blurb: Rose, red and white. Every loaded pad has a slow heartbeat; a press sends a pink pulse outward like a ripple in a cup of wine.

stars.name: Stars & Stripes
stars.blurb: Red, white and blue for the Fourth. Rows alternate like stripes; a press fires a firework cross along its row and column.

muertos.name: Dia de Muertos
muertos.blurb: Marigold, magenta and turquoise: the ofrenda. Empty pads rain slowly downward like petals; a press scatters marigold sparks.

synthwave.name: Synthwave
synthwave.blurb: Hot pink, violet and azure. The empty pads scan slowly like a horizon grid; a press fires a pink-to-azure shockwave.

newsprint.name: Newsprint
newsprint.blurb: Black and white only. Colour becomes brightness: the loud hues go white, the quiet ones grey. A press leaves a white ring that fades to ink.

inverse.name: Inverse
inverse.blurb: Black and white as a negative. Quiet pads glow, the playing pad goes dark, empty pads go white, and every press flips the whole grid for a beat.

darkside.name: Prism (Dark Side)
darkside.blurb: After the sleeve of Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon (1973): a white beam crosses the empty pads, hits the prism, and fans into a five-row spectrum. A pulse of light travels the whole way. A press throws rainbow rings.

pulsar.name: Pulsar (Unknown Pleasures)
pulsar.blurb: After the sleeve of Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures (1979), whose artwork plots the radio pulses of a pulsar as stacked white lines on black. Each row is a line; lumps rise out of the middle and are redrawn slowly. A press leaves a white ring that fades to ink.

kindofblue.name: Blue (Kind of Blue)
kindofblue.blurb: After Miles Davis's Kind of Blue (1959), in the one colour. Every empty pad breathes slowly between two blues; playing pads swell to white; a press sends a pale ring out through the blues.

purplerain.name: Purple Rain
purplerain.blurb: After Prince and the Revolution's Purple Rain (1984), in the one colour: violet and magenta fall slowly through the empty pads, playing pads pulse to purple, and a press scatters sparks.
